title: Finitely generated separable extensions are filtered colimits of smooth algebras
statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finitely generated separable extension of fields. Then $L$
is a filtered colimit of finitely generated smooth $K$-algebras, and the
colimit may be taken over smooth $K$-subalgebras of $L$ with the inclusions
as transition maps.

proof.text: (A smooth subalgebra with fraction field $L$.) Read "separable" in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] and "smooth" in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Since $L/K$ is finitely generated and separable, [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-fraction-field-of-smooth-algebra] gives a $K$-subalgebra $B\subseteq L$ such that $K\to B$ is smooth and every element of $L$ is $b/b'$ with $b,b'\in B$, $b'\neq0$; $B$ is a domain, being a subring of the field $L$.

(The localizations are smooth subalgebras.) For $0\neq f\in B$ let $B[1/f]=\{bf^{-m}:b\in B,m\ge0\}\subseteq L$. The map $B_f\to L$, $b/f^m\mapsto bf^{-m}$, from the localization of $B$ at $\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$ is well defined ($f$ is a unit of $L$), injective ($bf^{-m}=0$ forces $b=0$) with image $B[1/f]$, so $B_f\cong B[1/f]$ as $K$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization] applied to the smooth map $K\to B$ and $g=f$, $K\to B_f$ is smooth, hence so is $K\to B[1/f]$ (the conditions of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] are carried along a $K$-algebra isomorphism); in particular $B[1/f]$ is of finite presentation, so a finitely generated smooth $K$-subalgebra of $L$.

(Filtered colimit.) The subalgebras $B[1/f]$, $0\neq f\in B$, ordered by inclusion, form a directed family: $B[1/f]$ and $B[1/g]$ lie in $B[1/fg]$, and $fg\neq0$ since $B$ is a domain; the family is nonempty ($B=B[1/1]$). Its union is $L$, since each $b/b'\in L$ lies in $B[1/b']$. A directed union of subalgebras is their filtered colimit with the inclusions as transition maps, so $L=\operatorname{colim}_{f}B[1/f]$ is a filtered colimit of finitely generated smooth $K$-subalgebras of $L$ (Step 2) with inclusions as transition maps.
